newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Nigerian troops outnumbered at Freetown hotel.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian troops outnumbered at Freetown hotel.

text.p: Sierra Leonean rebels allied to coup soldiers massed around a Freetown hotel guarded by Nigerian troops on Monday after Nigeria intervened against the coup leaders.
Hotel guests and Nigerian soldiers said the Nigerians were hopelessly outnumbered and the hotel was about to be overrun. "It's a fight for survival," said one Nigerian officer.

A Reuters correspondent at the hotel said he saw a MiG jet of the Guinean airforce bombing positions of the rebel Revolutionary United Front (RUF). Guinea and Ghana have sent troops to support the Nigerian-led intervention.
"The Nigerians are outnumbered and outgunned, there is no sign or prospect of reinforcement. The RUF are massing closer and closer to the hotel," he said.
The hotel holds about 1,000 West African foreigners who took refuge their after the May 25 coup and a few foreign journalists.
Hundreds of foreigners fleeing looting and violence have been evacuated from the heliport in its grounds in the past few days.
